name: Long-Term Residence (EU long-term resident status)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 5 years of uninterrupted legal stay in Croatia (temporary stay, asylum, or subsidiary protection all count). Absences totalling no more than 10 months over the 5 years are permitted, or a single absence of up to 6 months. University study counts at half-time toward this period; seasonal work, posted-worker permits, trainee stays, and secondary-school attendance do not count at all.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years' continuous qualifying legal stay in Croatia.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires knowledge of the Croatian language and Latin script, unless under preschool age, educated in Croatia, or over 65 and not employed. Tested by university humanities faculties and approved institutions.
requirements.fix_path: Pass the required Croatian language and Latin-script test, or qualify for an exemption.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 5 years' continuous qualifying legal stay
Croatian language and Latin-script certificate (or exemption evidence)

sources.title: Ministarstvo unutarnjih poslova Republike Hrvatske (mup.gov.hr) -- Long-Term Residence and Permanent stay

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Croatia's initial build. This is the EU-directive 'long-term resident' status (distinct from Croatia's own domestic 'permanent stay'/stalni boravak -- see hr_permanent_stay -- which the same government page addresses as a related but separate status with different, narrower category-specific thresholds). language_local value is 'basic' rather than a CEFR letter grade because the source describes the test as institution-administered without stating a specific CEFR level (unlike Estonia's explicit B1). No language requirement applies to hr_permanent_stay per the same source -- a real, worth-noting distinction between the two Croatian settled statuses. prerequisites lists the routes that plausibly feed this status per the source's 'temporary stay, asylum, or subsidiary protection' language; the business route is included despite its own draft status/sourcing gaps since time spent under it, once granted, would count the same way.
